code: fit$jags_code ## model { ##   # mcp helper values ##   cp_0 = CONST1_ ##   cp_2 = CONST2_ ##  ##   # Priors for population-level effects ##   cp_1 ~ dunif(CONST1_, CONST2_)  # Within the observed change-point span ##   cp_1_sd ~ dnorm(0, 1/(197.7306)^2) T(0,)  # Group-level change-point variation ##   Intercept_1 ~ dt(23.4, 1/(7.2)^2, 3)   # Robustly centered mean intercept with a minimum scale of 2.5 ##   x_2 ~ dt(0, 1/(0.07282637)^2, 3)   # Regularizing mean coefficient scaled to a reference predictor change ##   sigma_1 ~ dt(0, 1/(7.2)^2, 3) T(0,)  # Positive residual SD calibrated on the response scale ##  ##   # Priors for group-level effects ##   for (id_ in 1:n_unique_id) { ##     cp_1_id_uncentered[id_] ~ dnorm(CONST3_, 1/(cp_1_sd)^2) T(CONST1_-cp_1,CONST2_-cp_1)  # Zero-mean ordered group-level change-point offsets ##   } ##   cp_1_id = cp_1_id_uncentered - mean(cp_1_id_uncentered)  # vectorized zero-centering ##  ##   # Model and likelihood ##   for (i_ in 1:length(x)) { ##     # par_x local to each segment ##     x_local_1_[i_] = min(x[i_], (cp_1 + cp_1_id[id[i_]])) ##     x_local_2_[i_] = min(x[i_], cp_2) - (cp_1 + cp_1_id[id[i_]]) ##      ##     # Formula for mu ##     link_mu_[i_] = ##      ##       # Segment 1: y ~ 1 ##       (x[i_] >= cp_0) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(1)], c(Intercept_1)) * 1 +  ##      ##       # Segment 2: y ~ 1 + (1 | id) ~ 0 + x ##       (x[i_] >= (cp_1 + cp_1_id[id[i_]])) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(2)], c(x_2)) * x_local_2_[i_] ##      ##     # Formula for sigma ##     link_sigma_[i_] = ##      ##       # Segment 1: y ~ 1 ##       (x[i_] >= cp_0) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(3)], c(sigma_1)) * 1 ##  ##     # Likelihood and log-density for family = gaussian() ##     mu_[i_] = link_mu_[i_] ##     sigma_[i_] = max(1e-03, link_sigma_[i_]) ##     y[i_] ~ dnorm(mu_[i_], 1 / sigma_[i_]^2) ##   } ## }

Understanding mcp formulas: Parameter names Intercept_i (intercepts), cp_i (change points), x_i (slopes), ar*/ma* (autocorrelation), sigma_* (Gaussian residual standard deviation). change point model basically ifelse model order constraints change points. Generate data supported models using fit$simulate(). See examples , e.g., mcp_example("demo")$example_code. Supported families link functions: mcp currently supports specific combinations families (gaussian(), binomial(), bernoulli(), poisson(), negbinomial()) link functions (identity, logit, probit, log). using informative priors incorporate expert knowledge. Use binomial(link = "logit") binomial change points mcp. Also relevant bernoulli(link = "logit"). Use negbinomial(link = "log") poisson(link = "log"). Read Poisson negative binomial change points mcp. Get results linear-predictor (link) scale rather response scale using plot(fit, scale = "linear") fitted(fit, scale = "linear"). Model comparison hypothesis testing: Leave-One-Cross-Validation using loo(fit) loo::loo_compare(loo1, loo2). Compute Savage-Dickey density ratios using hypothesis(fit, "cp_1 = 40"). Leverage directional conditional tests assess interval hypotheses (hypothesis(fit, "cp_1 > 30 & cp_1 < 50")), combined hypotheses (hypothesis(fit, "cp_1 > 30 & Intercept_1 > Intercept_2")), etc. Group-level (random) effects: Model group-level intercepts, slopes, change points using (1|id), (condition||id), +(condition|id). Get posteriors using ranef(fit). Plot using plot(fit, facet_by = "my_group") plot_pars(fit, pars = "group", type = "dens_overlay", ncol = 3). Default priors bound group-specific change points relative adjacent population-level change points. Modeling autoregression distributional parameters like Gaussian residual standard deviation: ~ 0 + sigma(1) models intercept change standard deviation. ~ 0 + sigma(0 + x) models increasing/decreasing standard deviation. Explicit sigma() formulas use log link, coefficients log-SD scale. ~ ar(N) models Nth order autoregression residuals. ~ar(N, 0 + x) models increasing/decreasing autocorrelation. can provide complete models distributional parameters (currently sigma(), shape(), mu()) time-series (ar() ma()). example, ~ x + sigma(1 + x:condition) models abrupt change followed -condition slopes variance. Informativeness increases number change points increase. Fix parameters specific values using cp_1 = 45 share parameters segments using slope_1 = "slope_2". text: mcp model continuous predictor \(x\), segment 1 (\(x \le \Delta_1\)) standard regression model intercept defined \(x = 0\): $$\eta_{1, } = f_1(x_i, \mathbf{\beta}_1) = \beta_{1,0} + \beta_{1,1} x_i + \dots$$ subsequent segments \(k \\{2, \dots, K\}\), change point \(\Delta_{k-1}\) marks onset new segment. model defines segment-local predictor \(X_{k,}\) measured segment onset \(\Delta_{k-1}\) capped segment end \(\Delta_k\): $$X_{k,} = \min(x_i, \Delta_k) - \Delta_{k-1}$$ \(\Delta_K = \max(\mathbf{x})\). local predictor \(X_{k,}\) zero segment onset (\(x_i \le \Delta_{k-1}\)) plateaus \(\Delta_k - \Delta_{k-1}\) \(x_i \ge \Delta_k\). Joined (continuous) segments (~ 0 + x) joined models, segment \(k \ge 2\) intercept specifies new segment slope \(\beta_{k,1}\): $$\eta_i = \eta_{1,}(X_{1,}) + \sum_{k=2}^K [x_i \ge \Delta_{k-1}] \cdot \beta_{k,1} X_{k,}$$ \(X_{1,} = \min(x_i, \Delta_1)\). earlier segments plateau boundary values, expectation automatically continuous across change points without requiring parameter constraints. joined disjoined segments, slope intercept parameters absolute values (differences relative previous segment). Disjoined (discontinuous) segments (~ 1 + x) segment \(k\) contains explicit intercept (\(\beta_{k,0}\)), introduces step change \(x_i = \Delta_{k-1}\) previous segments truncated \([x_i < \Delta_{k-1}]\). Extended formulas model features Distributional regression: Model residual variance distributional parameters across segments, e.g., ~ sigma(1 + x) ~ shape(1). Time-series residuals: Model serial dependence using ar(p) ma(q) terms generalized link-scale recurrence spans continuously across change points. Group-level effects: Add hierarchical (random) intercepts, slopes, change points, e.g., ~ 1 + (1|id) 1 + (1|id) ~ 0 + x. Model comparison hypothesis testing: Compare models using LOO-CV (loo(), waic()) test directional point-null hypotheses (hypothesis()) using Savage-Dickey density ratios. title: mcp 0.4.0
text: Multiple regression: mcp now supports several continuous predictors, categorical predictors, interactions, etc. terms RHS. E.g., ~ 1 + x + x:group + sigma(1 + group) + ar(2, 0 + z). Basically, now aims “feels” like lm() glm() distributional parameter segment. Explore ex = mcp_example("multiple") see action. Default priors generally align brms, adjustments accommodate change-point model. Group-level effects RHS: Predictor formulas now support group-level effects (sometimes called random effects) using familiar lme4 brms syntax. (1 | group) specifies group-level intercept, (1 + x || group) (factor || group) support independent coefficients, including slopes factors. also works inside distributional formulas sigma(1 + (factor || id)). ar(), effect carries later segments redefined disabled (0 | group). See mcp_example("group_mu") worked example. Correlated multi-coefficient terms yet supported. mcpfits now work natively R generics, posterior tidybayes posterior draw prediction API. Changes include: summary(fit) now reports rank-normalized split-rhat, ess_bulk, ess_tail posterior central quantile intervals instead HDIs. Adding as_draws(fit), as_draws_df(fit), tidy_draws(fit), ndraws(fit), rstantools linpred/epred, etc. full S3 generic registration posterior, rstantools, tidybayes (spread_draws(), gather_draws()). Per-draw methods (summary = FALSE fitted(), predict(), residuals(), log_lik()) now return dot-prefixed columns (.epred, .prediction, .residual, .loglik) tidybayes / ggdist compatibility. nsamples soft-deprecated favor ndraws; which_y deprecated favor dpar. Added R generics mcpfits: formula(fit), family(fit), model.frame(fit), nobs(fit), vcov(fit), confint(fit). Fits now also store proper matched $call. Printed summaries now report posterior sd new layout. Negative binomial GARMA: can now mcp(..., family = negbinomial()). Autoregression (ar()) generalized GARMA link-scale residuals Gaussian, binomial, Poisson, negative-binomial models default links, using ar(..., boundary = 0.1) default keep zero boundary counts finite. Added moving-average terms ma(q), can used alone combined ar(p) segment. Missing response imputation: Missing responses now retained posterior JAGS imputations. predict(fit) |> filter(.na(y)) can used see imputed values - similarly fitted(). supports AR/MA . Missing values AR/MA supported log_lik(), loo(), waic() throw informative error. See details new vignette/article missing data.

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: mcp v0.4 major breaking change aim remaining relatively stable going forward towards version 1.0. Although lot updated, parameter estimates v0.4.0 remain practically identical previous public release (v0.3.4). Deprecation detections added reach 1.0. Renamed parameters consistent brms: int_i –> Intercept_i; x_1_E2 –> xE2_1; x_1_sin –> sinx_1, etc. fit$pars removed. Use mcp_pars(fit) canonical table model parameters mcp_columns(fit) resolved data-column roles, including automatically chosen par_x. general, renamed "varying" "group". example names "varying_mu" "varying_cp" now "group_mu" "group_cp". plot_pars(), use pars = "group"; old "varying" selector remains deprecated alias. established varying = method argument remains unchanged now. summary(), fixef(), ranef(), prior_summary(), everything else now return rows canonical order instead previous incidental (near-alphabetical) order. Use verbose = TRUE summary(), fixef(), ranef() include segment dpar columns. Rhat renamed rhat summary(), fixef(), ranef(), match posterior standard. plot() now split plot() plotting full fits plot_dpar() plots one distributional parameter (mu, sigma, shape, ar1, etc.). argument order changed . new coloring function (plot(fit, color_by = "column")) particularly useful models include categorical predictors rhs group-level effects. See mcp_example("group_mu") worked example. hypothesis() now restricts equality tests simple parameter contrasts gives clearer guidance Savage-Dickey Bayes factors. Non-linear transformations hypotheses like x_1 / x_2 = 1 previously run, even though Savage-Dickey support . Equality tests now return p = NA Bayes factor model comparison, posterior parameter probability. Density estimates robust, warn evaluating Savage-Dickey Bayes factors default priors, warn sparse tails. fixef() now reports population-level effects mu (primary response parameter), excluding change points, distributional parameters, AR/MA parameters, group-effect SDs. Use summary(fit) get parameters. y | weights(w) now specifies brms-aligned observation log-likelihood weights rather Gaussian precision weights (previously scaled residual SD sigma / sqrt(w)). Predictive draws expectations now use sigma directly log_lik() multiplies observation log-densities w. Additionally, weight column longer removed fitted() predict() output observation weights remain available returned data. AR MA intercepts now zero-centered, regularizing dnorm(0, 0.5) T(-1, 1) priors, replacing independent uniform priors. categorical contrasts numeric slopes now use modest normal priors instead heavy-tailed Student-t priors. Coefficients remain direct jointly constrained stationary invertible regions. Gaussian models explicit sigma() formula now model residual standard deviation log link, brms. Models without explicit sigma() unchanged: sigma_1 remains residual SD response-scale half-Student-t prior. Formula transformations now use original predictor values, lm(), glm(), brms. Previously, transformations change-point predictor sin(x) exp(x) restarted segment onset. Bare par_x polynomial bases (par_x^2) remain segment-local support joined segment shapes. Group-level change points (1|id) remain exactly zero-centered identify population-level change points support efficient sampling. models multiple group-level change points, realized locations now constrained remain ordered. Read vignette group-level effects. sampling, mcp() now verifies population- group-level change points strictly ordered every draw population-level change points lie within observed predictor range. ordering broken, wrong segments apply. Parallel sampling now controlled exclusively active future plan. cores argument mcp() deprecated ignored, remains available backwards compatibility. Use future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 3) calling mcp() sample chains parallel, future::plan(future::sequential) shut workers. Without parallel future plan, chains sampled sequentially. mcp(..., adapt = 1000) soft-deprecated favor mcp(..., warmup = 1000) compatibility additional future samplers. Dropped support rel() formulas. ambiguous interaction terms made code hard maintain. Another way achieving functionality via priors may added future versions. arguments fit$simulate() changed accommodate multiple (categorical) predictors. fit$simulate(fit, data, ..., .type = "predict") new argument structure. Note (1) now requires fit first argument, (2) requires data.frame tibble second argument instead just vector par_x, (3) arguments prefixed “.” avoid name conflicts internally mcp. ... model parameters usual. Dropped support mcp(..., data = NULL). now must provide mock-data inform mcp types levels predictor columns. See, e.g., mcp_example("intercepts")$example_code simple example mcp_example("multiple")$example_code involved example. docs updated appropriately. mcp longer exports phi, logit, ilogit, probit. fit = mcp_example("name") now returns fit directly instead list $fit entry. now defaults sampling model (sample = "post") sample argument now directly passed mcp(..., sample = sample) sample = TRUE deprecated.

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: Added prior_summary(fit). compact output shows parameter’s resolved prior bounds; prior_summary(fit, verbose = TRUE) also shows data-dependent rule, plain-language description, source, kind (distribution, alias, expression, constant). Default priors now resolved JAGS code generated, fit$prior generated code longer depend opaque data constants. introduction multiple regression including categorical predictors (including distributional parameters) come default priors. non-par_x terms, numeric coefficients now auto-scaled data model. Briefly, based observed range two values, two standard deviations otherwise, aligning Gelman (2008) prior autoscaling rstanarm. See prior_summary(fit, verbose = TRUE) details. Default plot(fit) style updated many ways accommodate multiple regression group-effects. Added mcp(..., series = "data_column") identify independent series models AR/MA terms. Added option test hypotheses prior using hypothesis(fit, prior = TRUE). mcp_example(...) now shows illustrative plot fitted example default. Disable using plot = FALSE. Methods like fitted() predict() now accept fitted(fit, varying = "cp") fitted(fit, varying = "predictor") fast selectors group-level effects corresponding formula part. Exact group-level parameter names remain supported , varying = TRUE selects , ranef() continues return group-level effects. Added log_lik(fit) returns draws--observation matrix default. usual brms return shape accepted directly loo. log_lik() supports arguments e.g. fitted(). Memory improvement: mcpfit now < 10% size log-likelihood stored. Use log_lik(fit) compute , call loo(fit) waic(fit) directly. Sampling now 1-10% faster due new formalization underlying JAGS code. Use mcp(..., seed = 42) reproducible JAGS sampling. See mcp_example("demo")$example_code ensure reproducibility across simulation, fit, plotting. mcp(..., quiet = TRUE) suppresses routine JAGS output mcp sampling-status messages preserving warnings errors. Added warnings various thresholds exceeded. mcp(..., diagnostics = list(rhat = 1.01, ess_bulk = 400, ess_tail = 400, ar = 0.10, ma = 0.10)) controls fit diagnostics configurable thresholds. Partial lists override defaults, individual diagnostics can disabled NULL, diagnostics = FALSE disables diagnostic warnings. summary(fit) inherits settings accepts override diagnostic footer.
